subject: Evaluation playbook, recommended model shortlist, and next asks
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@noventis.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation playbook, recommended model shortlist, and next asks

Hi Samira —

Great to meet you and the Noventis team on today’s demo. Quick recap and a pragmatic evaluation path so we can get you a clear answer on cost/latency/quality tradeoffs within two weeks.

TL;DR recommendation (for your use case: clinical note summarization + triage prompts):
- Option A — LlamaX-13B (quantized int8): best balance of latency and cost for structured summaries. 95th p99 latency ~180ms/token on our Dedicated 1-GPU config, cost estimate ~0.6x of baseline. Quality: high for extractive summaries, occasional hallucination on rare entities.
- Option B — Redwood-Chat-30B (fp16, tuned): higher quality on nuanced instructions and multi-turn context, p99 latency ~420ms/token on 2-GPU config, cost ~2.1x baseline. Recommended if you prioritize overall concision + instruction following.
- Option C — MistralLite-7B (optimized): lowest cost and best throughput for high-volume triage classification; good for lightweight inference, but weaker on long-form summarization.

What we’re proposing next:
1) Redwood runs a 48-hour evaluation on your sample prompt set (attached) against Options A/B/C using your redaction rules. We’ll provide token-level latency & cost breakdowns plus a few representative transcripts. No charge for the trial.
2) We’ll deliver a one-page comparator (latency, cost, top-1 accuracy on your QA set, common failure modes) and a short recording of the eval run.
3) If results look good, we’ll scope an initial Dedicated reservation (1-2 GPUs) and a 30-day pilot with SLA and ingress controls.

Asks for you:
- Confirm the evaluation dataset (we received the de-identified sample v1 earlier; attached is noventis_prompt_set_v1.txt).
- Any hard P95 latency targets we must meet? You mentioned sub-300ms target for user-facing flows in the demo — confirm if that’s strict or aspirational.
- Procurement contacts to include for SOW/NDAs (I cc’d procurement if helpful).

Attachments: noventis_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt examples + redaction notes), redwood_demo_recording_link.txt (recording), redwood_benchmarks_summary_q1.csv (benchmarks excerpt).

I’ll hold 30 minutes on Thursday for a quick sync if you want to review the comparator live.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

---
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for predictable latency & cost
From: Samira Khan <samira@noventis.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@noventis.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation playbook, recommended model shortlist, and next asks

Thanks Camila — good summary. A few clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Data residency: we need to ensure logs and caches for the eval remain within US regions (we cannot send raw tokens outside US). Is the 48-hour eval runnable in our US-only Dedicated region?
2) P95 target: user-facing flows need P95 < 300ms end-to-end (including network hop) — backend token generation budget should aim for ~200ms P95. If Option B cannot meet that, we’ll likely focus on A or C.
3) SOC2 evidence: procurement asked for a SOC2 snapshot and redwood’s retention policy for log artifacts during the trial. Can you include a short packet?
4) For the dataset: the attached sample is fine. One ask — can you run the comparator with and without deterministic sampling (beam/greedy) so we can compare stability?

If you can confirm residency and SOC2 packet, we’ll give procurement a green light for the 48-hour test.

Best,
Samira
Director, Product Ops | Noventis HealthTech
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@noventis.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@noventis.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation playbook, recommended model shortlist, and next asks

Samira — thanks, good questions. Quick responses below and next steps.

- Residency: yes — we can run the full eval in our US-East Dedicated cluster (no egress). Logs and KV cache dumps will remain in your selected AWS account/region for the length of the test; we’ll purge snapshots within 7 days unless you request retention.
- Latency: preliminary internal tests show Option A (LlamaX-13B int8) p95 token generation ~160–220ms depending on sequence length; Option B is ~380–450ms; Option C ~100–140ms. We’ll include network delta in the report. If you require 200ms backend p95, Option A or C are the candidates.
- SOC2 and retention: attached SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf covers control mappings, retention policy, and contact for compliance. If your team needs a more formal package (AICPA letter), we can coordinate with security (usually a 48–72 hour turnaround).
- Deterministic vs stochastic: we’ll run both greedy/beam and temperature=0.7 sampling passes and surface stability metrics (lexical variance, top-k agreement).

Next steps we’ll take immediately once procurement confirms: schedule the eval to start 48 hours after confirmation, provision US-East Dedicated env, and deliver an interim snapshot after the first 12 hours. 

I’m attaching the prompt set and a short benchmark snippet in this reply for visibility.

Attachments: noventis_prompt_set_v1.txt, redwood_benchmarks_summary_q1.csv, SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf

If procurement approves today, we can kick off Wednesday evening PST.

Thanks —
Camila

Marissa, can you own the provisioning checklist and confirm that the US-East cluster has the patched kernel for LlamaX-13B int8 path? We should also flag the compliance request so security can prep the AICPA letter if procurement asks.
